questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to explore Australia while also focusing on my education

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an extremely good experience. I learned a lot from my classes and Melbourne is a super fun city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't need assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay-ish. I got an Airbnb for the first 10 days and found somewhere to live after about a week. However, I spent a lot of time refreshing Facebook, texting random people, and I was also open to any area in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The Fairy Floss real estate Facebook group is the way to go. The housing market moves very so you can definitely wait until you get to Melb but I also know of people that managed to find somewhere to live ahead of time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most houses are not insulated at all which means that it gets very cold indoors in the winter. I'd recommend bringing sweaters and indoor shoes.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you apply, you have to submit an excel file listing all the subjects you wish to take that have prerequisites along with proof that you fulfil them. Be careful with your choices as getting approved for subjects with prerequisites after the application process is an extremely tedious process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Didn't need help so don't know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the subjects I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The subject pages only offer limited information. Search up the subject codes online and read what other people are saying. The UniMelb page on Reddit is extremely active so chances are someone will have written something about your subject in the past

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Computer Vision: very challenging, Machine Learning Applications for Health: appropriately challenging, Database Systems & Information Modelling: homework-intensive but fairly easy, Management Competencies: very easy.

I spend way more time studying throughout the semester than I'd normally do at KU but I obviously wasn't working part-time like I do at home, so there's probably a bias there. I had two project-based exams that weren't too hard and two in-person no-aids exams that required A LOT of studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A similar format of large lecture + small tutorial classes. My tutors (TAs) were all PhD students in the field they were teaching and thus significantly better qualified than what I've experienced at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: COMP90086 Computer Vision, COMP90089 Machine Learning Applications for Health, INFO90002 Database Systems & Information Modelling, MGMT90140 Management Competencies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The computer science/informatics subjects I did were all very very good and I can recommend all of them. The teaching quality was great, better than anything I have experienced at uni in Denmark. Management Competences wasn't uninteresting but was unfortunately taught very poorly so I can't recommend it.
I can't speak for other fields but for IT-related study I really can't recommend UniMelb enough. It will make you wish you were doing your whole degree there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. Whatever you're into basically. Sports, music, cultural exchange etc. etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mountaineering club were a fun bunch.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other than exploring Melbourne, I did a three-day group trip to see Uluru which was one of the best experiences of my life. I'd also recommend renting a car and doing a weekend trip on the Great Ocean Road. If you're able to go, take a trip to see the Great Barrier Reef.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to your tutorials and chat with your classmates. There are a lot of international full-degree students and I ended up bonding with quite a few of them. The Aussies are very friendly but generally have their own friend groups and I found it harder to bond with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know if it can be called a cultural difference, but It's a very car-centric country in general. Public transport in Melb is okay but getting around outside of the city is hard without a car

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How laid-back the locals were. The Asian influence also meant really good food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for as many grants/scholarships as you can as they will fund all your adventures. Visit different suburbs as they are all so different and cool in their own way. Bring some warm clothes for the winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike for $120 from The Bike Shed in Brunswick my first weekend and really appreciated having it. Biking is not as safe as in Copenhagen so be careful. It is required by law to wear a helmet.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Despite how good academics were, the best part was definitely exploring Melbourne and the rest of Australia on my time off.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period was a bit rough but very rewarding and if you do a subject with an in-person exam you'll get to sit it in a museum.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
